stances.claim: Disini v. Republic (June 15, 2021), ably penned by Justice Ramon Paul L. Hernando in a 58-page unanimous decision, directed Herminio T. Disini to pay the Republic P1 billion in temperate damages and P1 million in exemplary damages plus 6% legal interest from finality -- recognizing that Disini acquired ill-gotten wealth via substantial commissions from Westinghouse and B&R on the 1976 BNPP project that 'remains inoperable to this day.'
stances.rhetorical_move: doctrinal-summary tribute (acknowledging the ponente and unanimous outcome)

stances.claim: Despite the unanimous finding of ill-gotten wealth, the Republic's lawyers failed to prove the actual receipt of the alleged P50.5 billion in commissions because they presented only a photocopy (instead of the original) of a private document listing the commissions, violating the Best Evidence Rule -- the Court therefore granted only temperate and exemplary damages, not the P50.5 billion claimed.
stances.rhetorical_move: evidentiary-failure analysis (focusing on the gap between liability finding and recovery)

stances.claim: 'Oh, when will our government lawyers learn how to prove their claims via the elementary rules of evidence that ordinary law students know by heart?' -- a familiar CJ lament across his ill-gotten wealth columns, with the Sept. 26 piece on the Marcoses cited as parallel example.

Disini's June 3, 2014 death during case pendency does not foreclose recovery because the decision recorded his substitution by his heir Herminio Angel E. Disini Jr. -- anticipating and resolving the from-whom-will-government-collect question.

The Disini case has a personal CJ history: PCGG v. Desierto (Feb. 10, 2003, CJ ponente) directed the Ombudsman to file criminal charges against Disini; CJ's March 27, 2011 Inquirer column lamenting that no one had been convicted or jailed for the BNPP fiasco triggered Disini's libel complaint against CJ and then-Inquirer editor in chief Letty Magsanoc -- dismissed by City Prosecutor Aspi, reversed by his temporary successor and filed without notice, then ultimately dismissed by the CA, DOJ, and Makati's new permanent prosecutor, all holding that 'no libel was committed by my citing correctly and quoting verbatim portions of a Supreme Court decision.'

While defending himself, CJ vowed to seek 'justice, even revenge' criminally, civilly, administratively, and ethically against the temporary city prosecutor, the lawyers who initiated the complaint, the RTC judge, and Disini himself -- but on reflection and prayer was led to Romans 12:19 ('Beloved, do not look for revenge but leave room for the wrath; for it is written, Vengeance is mine, I will repay, says the Lord') and set aside the vow, enjoying peace of mind in the Lord's promise.

notable_anecdotes: The full P50.5 billion-vs-P1.001 billion gap -- Court unanimously finds Disini acquired ill-gotten wealth, but Republic recovers only temperate + exemplary damages because evidence was a mere photocopy of a private document -- making this column the canonical CJ example of how the Best Evidence Rule defeats ill-gotten-wealth recovery in PCGG cases.

CJ's recurring exasperation line -- 'Oh, when will our government lawyers learn how to prove their claims via the elementary rules of evidence that ordinary law students know by heart?' -- a signature CJ-on-PCGG-lawyers register, with explicit cross-reference to his Sept. 26 piece 'Do the Marcoses have ill-gotten wealth?'.

Disini's death during case pendency (June 3, 2014) and substitution by heir Herminio Angel E. Disini Jr. -- preserving liability across the generational gap and resolving the from-whom-will-government-collect question in a single sentence of the decision.

The full libel-countersuit arc against CJ and Letty Magsanoc: Aspi dismissed → temporary successor reversed on reconsideration without notice → CA, DOJ, and new permanent prosecutor all re-dismissed, all holding 'no libel was committed by my citing correctly and quoting verbatim portions of a Supreme Court decision.' Among the most extended single-column accounts of CJ's personal litigation history.

CJ's vow-then-renunciation arc -- from 'I vowed to seek justice, even revenge' to 'I set aside my vow and enjoyed peace of mind in the Lord's promise' via Romans 12:19 -- one of the most explicit confessional turns in his column corpus, ending with 'To God be the glory always!' as benediction.
The BNPP itself 'remains inoperable to this day' -- 45 years after the 1976 award, the central physical-legacy datum of the entire Marcos-crony BNPP saga.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban discusses Disini v. Republic (June 15, 2021; full decision released only recently), the 58-page unanimous Supreme Court decision ably penned by Justice Ramon Paul L. Hernando directing Herminio T. Disini to pay the Republic P1 billion in temperate damages plus P1 million in exemplary damages plus 6% legal interest from finality -- recognizing that Disini, a close associate of Ferdinand E. Marcos, acquired ill-gotten wealth via substantial commissions from Westinghouse and Burns & Roe on the 1976 Bataan Nuclear Power Plant project that 'remains inoperable to this day.' However, the Republic's lawyers failed to prove the actual receipt by Disini of the alleged P50.5 billion in commissions because they presented only a photocopy (instead of the original) of a private document listing them, violating the Best Evidence Rule -- prompting CJ's recurring lament: 'Oh, when will our government lawyers learn how to prove their claims via the elementary rules of evidence that ordinary law students know by heart?' Disini's death on June 3, 2014 during the pendency of the case did not foreclose recovery because his heir Herminio Angel E. Disini Jr. was substituted in the suit. Panganiban then turns to the personal history of the case: in PCGG v. Desierto (February 10, 2003) he himself wrote the ponencia directing the Ombudsman to file criminal charges against Disini in the Sandiganbayan, and his March 27, 2011 Inquirer column lamenting that no one had been convicted for the BNPP fiasco triggered a libel complaint against him and then-Inquirer editor in chief Letty Magsanoc -- dismissed by City Prosecutor Feliciano Aspi, reversed without notice by his temporary successor on reconsideration, and ultimately re-dismissed by the Court of Appeals, the DOJ, and Makati's new permanent prosecutor, all holding 'no libel was committed by my citing correctly and quoting verbatim portions of a Supreme Court decision.' While defending himself, CJ vowed to seek 'justice, even revenge' criminally, civilly, administratively, and ethically against the temporary prosecutor, his cohorts, the RTC judge, and Disini himself -- but on reflection and prayer was led to Romans 12:19 ('Beloved, do not look for revenge but leave room for the wrath... Vengeance is mine, I will repay, says the Lord') and set aside the vow, enjoying peace of mind in the Lord's promise. 'To God be the glory always!'
